name: Yoruba
variant: Standard Yoruba (Nigeria), written with full tone marks and underdots
script: Latin with extra letters: ẹ, ọ, ṣ, the digraph gb, and tone marks (á, à) on vowels and syllabic n; left to right
basis: University of Florida YOR1130 Beginning Yoruba (Fall 2021) on Schleicher's Jẹ́ K'Á Sọ Yorùbá: preliminary lesson (greetings, alphabet and tones, numbers), then introductions and pronouns, family and yes/no questions, likes and the progressive, the home and 'to be', nationality and age with object pronouns, describing, then future, relatives, perfect and habitual
src: University of Florida, YOR1130 Beginning Yoruba syllabus (Fall 2021), textbook: A. Y. F. Schleicher, Jẹ́ K'Á Sọ Yorùbá (Yale University Press, 1993); week-by-week schedule, preliminary lesson and lessons 1-8
note: The order of greetings, alphabet and tones, numbers, introductions and pronouns, family, yes/no questions and negation, the progressive and likes, wà and 'to be', commands, nationality and age, object pronouns, describing and colours, future, tí, the perfect ti / kò tíì and the habitual máa ń / kì í follows the UF schedule. The syllabus summary I read had broken tone marks, so every Yoruba form in the titles is written from my own knowledge, not copied. Food and ordering, prices and the market, clock time and directions are not in the schedule and are added by common course practice. Merging and splitting the schedule's weeks into 26 lessons is my own judgment.
hardest: Three tones that change meaning: ọkọ̀ (vehicle), ọkọ (husband), ọkọ́ (hoe)
The underdot letters ẹ, ọ, ṣ, nasal vowels (an, ẹn, in, ọn, un) and the double stops gb and p
Respect built into grammar: ẹ for elders and strangers, o for friends, and greetings for every occasion
No verb endings: time and aspect come from small markers (ń, ti, máa, máa ń) and 'to be' has several words (ni, jẹ́, wà)

items: yo-alphabet
The alphabet: seven vowels with ẹ and ọ, ṣ, and the double stops gb and p
yo-tones
Three tones: high á, mid a, low à (ọkọ̀, ọkọ, ọkọ́) and nasal vowels
yo-greetings
Greetings by time of day: Ẹ káàárọ̀, Ẹ kú ọ̀sán, Ẹ kú ìrọ̀lẹ́
yo-respect
Respect: ẹ and o for 'you', Ẹ ṣé / O ṣé, and Ẹ kú + noun (Ẹ kú iṣẹ́, Ẹ kú àbọ̀)
yo-numbers
Numbers 1-20: ọ̀kan, èjì, ẹ̀ta … ẹ̀wá, ogún
yo-intro
Introducing yourself: Orúkọ mi ni…, Kí ni orúkọ rẹ?
yo-pronouns
Subject pronouns mo, o, ó, a, ẹ, wọ́n and possessives mi, rẹ, rẹ̀
yo-family
Family: bàbá, ìyá, ẹ̀gbọ́n and àbúrò (older and younger sibling)
yo-yes-no
Yes/no questions with ṣé, and Bẹ́ẹ̀ ni / Bẹ́ẹ̀ kọ́
yo-negation
Negation with kò and ò: Kò dára, Mi ò mọ̀
yo-numbers-big
Numbers 21-100, counting by twenty: ọgbọ̀n, ogójì, ọgọ́rùn-ún
yo-progressive
The progressive ń and likes: Mo ń jẹun, Mo fẹ́ràn…, Mo fẹ́…
yo-wa
wà: being somewhere, and the home (Níbo ni … wà?, ilé, yàrá)
yo-ni
'To be' with ni and jẹ́: Olùkọ́ ni mí, Ó jẹ́ dókítà
yo-commands
Commands and 'don't': Jókòó, Wá, Má lọ
yo-nationality
Nationality and age: Ọmọ Amẹ́ríkà ni mí, Ọmọ ọdún mélòó ni ọ́?
yo-object
Object pronouns: Ó rí mi, Mo rí i, Mo rí wọn
yo-describing
Describing with verbs (Ó ga, Ó dára) and colours: pupa, funfun, dúdú
yo-food
Food and ordering: oúnjẹ, omi, Mo fẹ́…, Ẹ jọ̀ọ́
yo-market
Prices and the market: Èló ni?, Mélòó?, náírà
yo-time
Days and clock time: Ọjọ́ Ajé, Ọjọ́ Ìṣẹ́gun; Aago mélòó ni?
yo-future
Future with máa and yóò: Mo máa lọ, Ó máa wá
yo-ti-relative
tí: who, which, when (ohun tí, ìgbà tí) and Nígbà wo?
yo-perfect
Done and not yet: Mo ti jẹun, Mi ò tíì jẹun
yo-habitual
Habits: máa ń and kì í (Mo máa ń lọ, Mi kì í lọ)
yo-transport
Transport and directions: wọ̀ ọkọ̀, gùn kẹ̀kẹ́, ọ̀tún, òsì
